title: oxyria digyna subsp. elatior
intro: Oxyria digyna subsp. elatior, commonly known as the Alpine Waterwort or Alpine Pearlwort, is a subspecies of the Oxyria digyna plant, which is a type of flowering plant in the buckwheat family (Polygonaceae). It is native to the high-altitude regions of Europe, Asia, and North America, where it can be found growing in wet environments such as marshes and streams. The Alpine Waterwort has been traditionally used for its medicinal properties, with reported health benefits including anti-inflammatory and antioxidant effects, which may help to reduce symptoms of arthritis and other inflammatory conditions. The therapeutic actions of Oxyria digyna subsp. elatior are attributed to its bioactive constituents, which include flavonoids, alkaloids, and glycosides, among others, although further research is needed to fully understand its medicinal properties.
